result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers agree that the forced 40-shortcut tour is wrong, give reasons grounded in these users, and propose much the same remedies: menu and tooltip hints, behavior-triggered nudges, a command palette, a cheat sheet and a short optional starter set. B wins narrowly because it gives a clearer rule for choosing the starter shortcuts (the ones used in every session) and a ready-made compromise for the PM. A's point about consistent key mappings is a real plus, and its length is about the same, so the gap is small. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers agree with the user and propose similar approaches: contextual hints, a command palette, a cheat sheet and a small skippable day-one set. B edges ahead because it states its recommendation up front, ties its reasons more closely to these users (experts in the app all day, the paralegal juggling matters) and makes the day-one start explicitly optional. B also adds two useful points: keeping the forty key mappings consistent, and measuring unaided shortcut use instead of tour completion.
